chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Walid al-Adl narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hatam narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Marrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said:

Four [characteristics] are such that whoever possesses all of them is a hypocrite; and if one of them is found in him, it is a characteristic of hypocrisy in him until he gives it up: whoever, when he speaks, lies; and when he promises, breaks his promise; and when he makes a pledge, betrays trust; and when he disputes, acts unjustly/transgresses.
ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics of a hypocrite in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, establishes a gradation of hypocrisy (*nifāq*) where the presence of even one trait indicates a lingering defect until rectified. The four characteristics—lying in speech, breaking promises, betraying pledges, and transgressing in disputes—correspond to the *khawāss* (specific traits) of the hypocrites mentioned in the Quran, distinguishing them from general believers. In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the concept of *nifāq al-ʿamal* (hypocrisy of action), emphasizing that outward piety is insufficient if these internal moral failings persist.
